## What's new in 0.1.0-preview.2
This second preview turns the GUI from a campground lookup into the place where you set Campertron up: it edits your settings, creates and edits your searches, lets you pick their filters from the campground's own data, and runs them when you ask and shows what they found. Its window is now organized in four tabs, Searches, Results, Settings and Campgrounds, and you can choose a light or dark theme for it. Every filter list now keeps or leaves out a campsite that matches **any** of its values, and a search can match its filter values exactly. The console searches as before otherwise; it gains earlier checks of your settings files and a fix for its menu. Your settings, search files, campground list and `Camp.History` keep working as they are; "Upgrading from 0.1.0-preview.1" below lists the few cases where something now behaves differently.

### Four tabs, in the order you use them
- The GUI's window now has four tabs: **Searches**, **Results**, **Settings** and **Campgrounds**. It opens on **Searches**.
- **Campgrounds** is the campground lookup, with a tab for each way to look: **By Park**, **By City** and **By State**. In 0.1.0-preview.1 these three were the GUI's only tabs.
- **Settings** has two tabs of its own: **Campertron** for `General.yaml` and `Email.yaml`, and **System** for the GUI's theme.
- Each tab keeps what you chose or typed while you look at another one.
- With the keyboard, the arrow keys switch between the tabs of a row, and Tab and Shift+Tab move through both rows of tabs and every field of the window.

### Run your searches in the GUI
- The new **Results** tab lists your search files with a check box each. Searches that run at startup are selected; the others are listed as "Not run at startup" and run only if you select them. A file that can't be searched, or that has unsaved changes in the Searches tab, says why.
- **Start** searches the selected files once, with the same search the console uses, and shows its progress. **Cancel** stops it at any time.
- The results show each search's status and counts and which months were checked, then the open sites grouped by date, or by site with their stays when you ask for consecutive nights. Choose a site to open its booking page on recreation.gov or to copy its ID or link.
- A month that recreation.gov did not answer is listed as "not checked", never as fully booked. Each month is asked for at most three times.
- If recreation.gov limits the requests, the search stops, keeps what it found, and **Start** waits five minutes. The GUI never exits because of it.
- The Results tab never changes your files, never sends email and doesn't use `Camp.History`, so it always shows every open site that matches right now. To be notified around the clock, keep using the console's email mode.

### Create and edit searches in the GUI
- The new **Searches** tab lists your search files and whether each one runs. It edits every setting of a search: the name, the dates, the days of the week, the number of people, the filters (see the next section), and the number of consecutive nights.
- Choose the campground from a list of every campground you can reserve (search by name, city, state, park or ID), or enter its exact ID. An ID that isn't in the campground list is reported before you save.
- **New search** creates a search from the example, switched off until you check **Run this search (autoRun)**. **Save as** saves a copy under a new name. Neither ever writes over an existing file, and nothing in the GUI deletes a file.
- Problems are shown next to the setting they belong to, and a preview shows exactly the lines a save will change.

### Pick filter values from the campground's data
- In the Searches tab, each of the eight filter lists (equipment, campsites, attributes and campsite types, each to include or to exclude) is a check list of the chosen campground's own values from Campertron's campground list, with how many campsites have each. Check the values you want; nothing is downloaded for this.
- Attributes are listed under their names (for example **Shade** with **Yes** and **No**). A campsite name that several campsites share is listed once, with how many share it. Long lists have a find box and **Select all shown** and **Clear shown**.
- Spellings that differ only in upper and lower case (such as `Yes` and `yes`) are grouped; checking the group adds every spelling.
- A value the campground doesn't have, such as one typed by hand, one from another campground or one that is no longer in the data, is kept in the file and shown under the list with what it matches, until you remove it. You can also type a value yourself; it is written exactly as you typed it.
- Checking a value adds it at the end of the list in the file; your comments, the order of the other values and their spelling stay as they are.
- With the keyboard, each list is one stop for Tab: the arrow keys move through its values and Space checks or unchecks one.

### Filters: any value matches, and you choose how
- An include list keeps a campsite that matches **any** of its values, and an exclude list leaves out a campsite that matches **any** of its values, in all eight lists. Before, `excludeEquipment` and `excludeAttributes` left a campsite out only if it matched **every** value, and `includeCampsiteType` kept a campsite only if its type matched **every** value; the other lists already worked this way.
- The new search setting `filterMatching` says how a value matches. **`Exact`**: the value must equal the campsite's equipment type, campsite name, `Name:Value` attribute or campsite type. **`Contains`**: the matching used before, in which a campsite type matches when it contains the value (`GROUP` matches `GROUP STANDARD NONELECTRIC`) and an equipment or attribute value matches when it contains the campsite's (`RV/MOTORHOME` matches a campsite that allows `RV`, and `Shade:Yes` also matches a campsite whose `Shade` is blank). Campsite names always match exactly, and upper and lower case, spaces and punctuation always count.
- A search file without `filterMatching`, which is every file written before this version, uses `Contains`, so its values keep matching as before. New searches, the example search included, are created with `Exact`; the example lists Watchman's group campsite type in full instead of `GROUP`, and finds the same campsites.
- The GUI's **Matching** choice sets `filterMatching` only when you choose it, and shows next to a value what else it matches with `Contains`. Opening or saving a file never adds `filterMatching` by itself.

### Edit your settings in the GUI
- The new **Settings > Campertron** tab edits `General.yaml` and `Email.yaml`: it says what each setting does, shows problems next to the setting, and previews the lines a save will change.
- The email password is masked on screen and never appears in the preview or in a message. You can reveal it while you type; it is hidden again when you save or leave. It is still stored in `Email.yaml` as plain text, as before. An `Email.yaml` that the GUI creates on Linux or macOS can be read only by your user.

### A light or dark window
- **Settings > System** chooses the GUI's theme: **System**, **Light** or **Dark**. **System** is the default and follows your computer's light or dark setting, as the GUI did before. **Light** and **Dark** always use that theme.
- Your choice applies at once and is kept for the next start. It is saved for your user account in `CampertronGUI/preferences.json`, next to the `CampertronConfig` folder, not in your settings files, and the console doesn't use it.
- If the saved choice can't be used, the GUI uses **System** and says so in **Settings > System** until you choose again.

### Your files stay yours
- Saving from the GUI changes only the lines you edited. Your comments, blank lines, order and formatting stay as you wrote them.
- Every save of an existing file leaves the previous version next to it with `.bak` added to its name, for example `General.yaml.bak` (one backup per file; a newer save replaces it). Campertron doesn't read `.bak` files as searches.
- If another program changes a file while you edit it, the GUI doesn't write over that change: it shows a conflict and lets you apply your edits to the new version or discard them.
- A file the GUI can't edit safely, for example one with an unknown setting, opens read-only with the reason. Campertron never rewrites a file to make it editable.
- Refreshing the campground list (**Refresh Ridb Data** or `autoRefresh`) now changes only the `lastRidbDataRefresh` line of `General.yaml`. Before, the refresh rewrote the whole file and removed your comments.
- Settings files are replaced in one step, so a crash or an error during a save leaves either the old file or the new one, never half of one.

### Campgrounds with the same name are told apart
- Every campground in the GUI's lists now shows its location and its ID, and the details always belong to the campground you chose. Before, for the few names that several campgrounds share, the GUI could show the details and ID of another campground with the same name. This was a known limitation of 0.1.0-preview.1.
- **By Park** (under **Campgrounds**) now also lists a park's campgrounds that have no address in the campground list.

### Settings problems are found before the search
- Email mode now checks `Email.yaml` when it starts. If the server, the port, the sender or the recipients are missing or unusable, Campertron says which and exits with code 1 before it searches. Before, it found out only when it tried to send the first email, after a complete search. Nothing is connected or sent by this check. This was a known limitation of 0.1.0-preview.1.
- A few settings that used to make Campertron hang, fail in the middle of a search or download the campground list at every start are now reported at start, with the file name, and Campertron exits with code 1. In a search that runs: a negative `searchValue` for `DaysOut` or `MonthsOut`, an empty item in an equipment, attribute or site-type list, or a `searchBy` number that has no meaning. In `General.yaml`: an `outputTo` number that has no meaning, or, with `autoRefresh: true`, a `refreshRidbDataDayInterval` that is not a real number.
- The new `filterMatching` setting is checked the same way. In a search that runs, a `filterMatching` that isn't written `Exact` or `Contains` (for example empty, a number or two values), or that is written twice, is reported at start with the file name, and Campertron exits with code 1. The GUI's Results tab doesn't run such a search, enabled or not.
- Which file is `General.yaml`, which is `Email.yaml` and which are searches no longer depends on your regional settings. Before, with Turkish regional settings, a file named `EMAIL.yaml` was read as a search file and refused.

### A faster first search of a campground
- The first search of a campground prepares its campsites' details. That used to read the whole list of campsite attributes once per campsite: about 3.7 seconds for Watchman Campground (192 campsites) and 6.6 seconds for the largest campground (360 campsites) when measured. It now takes less than a tenth of a second, because Campertron adds an index to its campground list. The GUI's filter lists use it too.
- The index makes `RecreationDotOrg.db` about 35 MB larger (about 262 MB instead of 226 MB). Campertron builds it once, at the first start after upgrading (about 0.7 seconds when measured; the GUI shows "Preparing campground data" meanwhile), and every refresh of the campground list builds it again. If it can't be built, for example because the file is read-only, everything works as before, only slower, and the next start tries again.

### A console menu that keeps working
- The menu no longer stops working after many key presses. Before, every key press, also keys the menu doesn't use, took a little more memory that was never given back, and after several thousand key presses (for example a key held down for several minutes) the console ended with a "Stack overflow" error.

### Checks before publishing
The release workflow must pass all of the following before it can publish this release; if any of them fails, nothing is published:
- all automated tests, none of which needs recreation.gov any more, and a scan that finds no known vulnerable packages;
- every download contains .NET 11, and all 16 downloads were compiled by the same .NET 11 compiler;
- the console and GUI downloads are started on Linux x64, Linux on ARM64, Windows x64, Windows on ARM, macOS on Intel and macOS on Apple silicon, and the 32-bit Windows downloads on 64-bit Windows: the console's version check and a first start that sets up the campground list, and the GUI's built-in smoke test. That test now also checks the four tabs, saves settings, a search file and a theme choice in a temporary folder, switches the window to the light and the dark theme, reads a campground's filter values without blocking the window and checks that the first start built the new index, and runs a search against stand-in data, without contacting recreation.gov. Linux on ARM64 and the 32-bit Windows downloads are new in this list;
- both Docker images, amd64 and arm64, start. Before, only the amd64 image was started;
- the checksums of all 16 downloads are generated and verified.

## Upgrading from 0.1.0-preview.1
- **Desktop:** extract the new archives and use them instead of your old Campertron folders. Your settings, searches, campground list and `Camp.History` (in the `CampertronConfig` data folder) are kept and need no changes.
- **Docker:** change the image tag to `0.1.0-preview.2` and recreate the container with the same `/config` and `/cache` mounts. There is no `latest` tag for pre-release versions, so the tag has to be changed by hand.
- **The GUI opens on Searches:** the campground lookup it used to open on is under **Campgrounds**, and your settings are under **Settings > Campertron**.
- **If you use email mode:** an incomplete `Email.yaml` now stops Campertron at the start with exit code 1 instead of at the first email. Fill in `Email.yaml` before you switch to `outputTo: Email`; **Settings > Campertron** in the GUI shows what is missing.
- **If a search file lists two or more values in `excludeEquipment`, `excludeAttributes` or `includeCampsiteType`:** it can find different campsites. An exclude list with several values can leave out more campsites (one matching value is enough), and an `includeCampsiteType` with several types now finds campsites of any of those types, not only campsites whose type contains all of them. Check these lists in the GUI's Searches tab; nothing in the file changes unless you save it.
- **Your existing searches keep `Contains` matching** because they have no `filterMatching`. To match values exactly, choose **Exact** under **Matching** in the Searches tab (or add `filterMatching: Exact`), and check that each value is spelled as the campground writes it: the GUI lists the values it doesn't find.
- **First start after upgrading:** Campertron adds an index to `RecreationDotOrg.db` (about 35 MB more disk space; about 0.7 seconds when measured). Earlier versions can still use the file.
- **If a search file has one of the settings listed under "Settings problems are found before the search":** Campertron now names the file and exits with code 1 at the start. Correct the setting, or open the file in the GUI's Searches tab to see the problem.
- **New files in the settings folder:** backups such as `General.yaml.bak` appear next to the files that the GUI or a refresh has changed. You can delete them at any time.
- **Theme choice:** when you choose a theme in **Settings > System**, the GUI creates `CampertronGUI/preferences.json` next to the `CampertronConfig` folder, not in it. Until you choose, nothing is created and the GUI follows your computer's theme as before.
- **Windows:** Campertron doesn't change a settings file that is read-only, is a link, or has permissions of its own instead of the folder's. The GUI then says why it can't save, and after a refresh the console warns that `General.yaml` could not be updated; the refreshed campground list is kept, and with `autoRefresh: true` the next start may refresh again.
- To check your download, use the checksums and build attestations described under "Verify your download" below.

## Known limitations
- **The GUI's tabs and themes on Windows and macOS.** The new layout, the filter check lists and the Settings, Searches and Results tabs were looked at and used by a person only on Linux. On Windows and macOS the checks before publishing start the GUI, run its built-in smoke test, read a campground's filter values and switch it to the light and the dark theme, but nobody has yet checked how the tabs look, their keyboard use or screen readers there, or whether **System** follows the theme setting of Windows and macOS.
- **Checking hundreds of filter values before saving.** Each change re-checks every value you added since the last save, so after checking all 360 campsites of a large campground (for example with **Select all shown**), each further change takes about a second until you save. After saving, a change takes a moment again.
- **Console on Windows and macOS.** As in 0.1.0-preview.1: the console's layout, colors and menu had a manual visual check on Windows, not a complete test, and haven't been tried on macOS. The menu fix of this version was checked in Linux terminals.
- **The Results tab can take a few minutes when recreation.gov doesn't answer.** A month is asked for up to three times, with a wait of 30 seconds after a failed request, before it is listed as "not checked". **Cancel** ends the wait at once.
- **Searching one campground for the first time in two Campertron programs at once.** The first search of a campground prepares its site details in `CampertronCache`. If the console and the GUI, or two consoles, do that for the same campground at the same moment, one can read a file the other is still writing, and that search can then stop with an error. This has not been seen in testing. If it happens, run the search again; to avoid it, let the first search of a campground finish in one program before you search it in another.
- **Email mode keeps running without any search to run.** If none of your search files has `autoRun: true`, email mode warns once and then reports "0 searches" at every check. The GUI's Searches tab shows the same warning.
- **Email clients not yet checked.** The results page was checked in Chrome and Firefox on Linux, but no test email was sent, so its appearance in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail is unverified. Each email contains the page twice (as the body and as the attachment), so a search with thousands of results can make a large email that some providers may reject.
- Avalonia, the GUI's UI framework, lists 32-bit Windows (`win-x86`) as a commercially supported platform only and doesn't list 32-bit ARM Linux desktops (`linux-arm`). The 32-bit Windows downloads are started on 64-bit Windows before publishing, not on a 32-bit system, and the `linux-arm` downloads are built but not started.
